newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen down on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen down on Thursday.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Wednesday but gains by heavyweights pushed the WIG index to a fourth straight 30-month high and analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing augured a profit-taking correction.
"It should be a classic correction -- nothing has changed since the start of our recent growth," said Artur Nagorka of Wood & Company.

Analysts said the main market could fall a few hundred points over one to three sessions but should soon resume growth to above 15,000 points, especially if firms' August earnings reports, most due on Wednesday, prove good.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 23.2 points to 14,832.7 and turnover rose 7.6 percent to 170.6 million zlotys ($61.3 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 43 to 20 with 14 stocks flat.
The WIG has jumped 9.3 percent over the last eight sessions.
Banks, which comprise about 40 percent of the main market's capitalisation, were expected to continue to post strong earnings and to continue to push the WIG upward.
Large-cap banks BRE, BIG and BPH rose 4.9 percent, 2.8 percent and 1.9 percent respectively.
Analysts said top-gaining small-cap Kredyt Bank, up 5.3 percent, may have been helped by the news it had finalised an eight-million-zloty ($2.9 million) real estate sale.
Analysts said Bank Komunalny, which started trade on the main market 59 percent above issue, could keep on rising along with the main market.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.4 million zlotys ($0.5 million) with biggest mover steel trader Stalexport down five percent.
